question_html: Accounting policies refer to:

options.A: Specific accounting principles and methods of applying those principles adopted by the enterprise
options.B: Random estimates made by external auditors at year-end
options.C: Tax computation guidelines mandated solely by the Income Tax Department
options.D: Daily cash flow budgets prepared by junior clerks

answer_html: Answer: (A) Specific accounting principles and methods of applying those principles adopted by the enterprise[cite: 51].

question_html: Why is there no single, unified list of accounting policies applicable to all enterprises in all circumstances?

options.A: Because enterprises operate in diverse and complex environmental situations requiring considerate management judgement
options.B: Because accounting standards explicitly forbid standardizing policies across industries
options.C: Because different businesses use different currencies
options.D: Because statutory laws change every week

answer_html: Answer: (A) Because enterprises operate in diverse and complex environmental situations requiring considerate management judgement[cite: 51].

question_html: Which of the following are illustrative areas where different accounting policies are frequently encountered?

options.A: Valuation of Inventories and Valuation of Investments
options.B: Employee dress code and office seating arrangement
options.C: Selection of advertising agency and media channel
options.D: Choice of office building color scheme

answer_html: Answer: (A) Valuation of Inventories and Valuation of Investments[cite: 51].

question_html: What are the three major characteristics that should be considered for the selection and application of accounting policies?

options.A: Prudence, Substance over form, and Materiality
options.B: Speed, Cost, and Profitability
options.C: Liquidity, Solvency, and Leverage
options.D: Size, Age, and Location of enterprise

answer_html: Answer: (A) Prudence, Substance over form, and Materiality[cite: 51].

question_html: Can the disclosure of an inappropriate or wrong accounting treatment rectify that inappropriate treatment?

options.A: Yes, full disclosure makes any accounting treatment legally valid
options.B: No, disclosure is necessary in any case, but disclosure cannot rectify a wrong or inappropriate treatment
options.C: Yes, provided the auditors sign off on it
options.D: Only if approved by shareholders in an AGM

answer_html: Answer: (B) No, disclosure is necessary in any case, but disclosure cannot rectify a wrong or inappropriate treatment[cite: 51].

question_html: Under which of the following conditions should a change in accounting policies be made?

options.A: When required by some statute or for compliance with an Accounting Standard, or when the change results in a more appropriate presentation of financial statements
options.B: Whenever management wants to boost profit figures to impress shareholders
options.C: Every year to keep auditors busy
options.D: Only when the company changes its business premises

answer_html: Answer: (A) When required by some statute or for compliance with an Accounting Standard, or when the change results in a more appropriate presentation of financial statements[cite: 51].

question_html: If an enterprise changes its inventory valuation formula from weighted average to FIFO, what is required regarding the financial statements?

options.A: The effect of such change on financial statement items must be quantified and disclosed
options.B: The change must be kept confidential from users
options.C: All prior years' balance sheets must be destroyed
options.D: No disclosure or quantification is necessary

answer_html: Answer: (A) The effect of such change on financial statement items must be quantified and disclosed[cite: 51].

question_html: Accounting policy for inventories of Xeta Enterprises states that inventories are valued at lower of cost determined on weighted average basis or net realizable value. Which accounting principle is primarily reflected here?

options.A: Prudence
options.B: Materiality
options.C: Substance over form

answer_html: Answer: (A) Prudence[cite: 51].

question_html: Selection of an inappropriate accounting policy may lead to:

options.A: Understatement or overstatement of financial performance and financial position
options.B: Exact balancing of trial balance without errors
options.C: Immediate tax exemption from the government

answer_html: Answer: (A) Understatement or overstatement of financial performance and financial position[cite: 51].

question_html: Omega Enterprises revised its accounting policy relating to inventory valuation to include applicable production overheads, believing it gives a more appropriate presentation. This change is:

options.A: Fully justified as it results in a more appropriate presentation of financial statements
options.B: Illegal under ICAI guidelines
options.C: Prohibited unless approved by tax authorities first

answer_html: Answer: (A) Fully justified as it results in a more appropriate presentation of financial statements[cite: 51].

question_html: Which body in India has been actively trying to reduce the number of acceptable accounting policies through Guidance Notes and Accounting Standards?

options.A: ICAI (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India)
options.B: Stock Exchange Board
options.C: Reserve Bank of India alone

answer_html: Answer: (A) ICAI (The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India)[cite: 51].

question_html: True or False: There is a single list of accounting policies applicable to all enterprises in all circumstances.

options.A: True
options.B: False

answer_html: Answer: (B) False[cite: 51].

question_html: Long-term investments are typically valued at their acquisition cost, and provision is made for:

options.A: Permanent diminution in value wherever necessary
options.B: Every minor daily stock market fluctuation
options.C: Inflation rates announced by the government

answer_html: Answer: (A) Permanent diminution in value wherever necessary[cite: 51].

question_html: If an enterprise adopts a policy where finished goods are valued at lower of cost or market value, and by-products are valued at net realizable value, this demonstrates:

options.A: Selection of specific accounting policies suited to specific items under appropriate circumstances
options.B: Violation of all fundamental accounting assumptions
options.C: An arbitrary guessing method without standards

answer_html: Answer: (A) Selection of specific accounting policies suited to specific items under appropriate circumstances[cite: 51].

question_html: Choosing FIFO or weighted average method for inventory valuation is an example of:

options.A: Selection of accounting policy
options.B: Tax evasion
options.C: Capital budgeting error

answer_html: Answer: (A) Selection of accounting policy[cite: 51].

question_html: What is the effect of changing an accounting policy on financial statements without quantifying its impact?

options.A: The financial statements may fail to help users of accounts properly interpret performance
options.B: Net profit automatically becomes zero
options.C: Tax liability is permanently waived

answer_html: Answer: (A) The financial statements may fail to help users of accounts properly interpret performance[cite: 51].

question_html: If an enterprise capitalizes interest which was earlier not in practice, what potential impact does this have on the financial statements?

options.A: It may materially increase net profit and asset values for the current period
options.B: It has zero impact on any financial statement item
options.C: It eliminates all liabilities

answer_html: Answer: (A) It may materially increase net profit and asset values for the current period[cite: 51].

question_html: Financial statements should be prepared on the basis of accounting policies that exhibit:

options.A: A true and fair view of the state of affairs (Balance Sheet and Profit & Loss Account)
options.B: The absolute minimum tax payable to the government
options.C: The highest possible share price on the stock market

answer_html: Answer: (A) A true and fair view of the state of affairs (Balance Sheet and Profit & Loss Account)[cite: 51].

question_html: True or False: Selection of an accounting policy impacts the financial performance and financial position of a business.

options.A: True
options.B: False

answer_html: Answer: (A) True[cite: 51].

question_html: Which of the following best describes why management judgement is required in choosing accounting policies?

options.A: Because different policies affect performance measurement and financial position differently, requiring choices appropriate to specific operating circumstances
options.B: Because management is legally required to change policies every month
options.C: Because tax auditors demand personal preferences
options.D: Because accounting software requires manual entry of policy codes

answer_html: Answer: (A) Because different policies affect performance measurement and financial position differently, requiring choices appropriate to specific operating circumstances[cite: 51].

question_html: A change in accounting policy is justified when:

options.A: It complies with accounting standards/law or ensures more appropriate presentation of financial statements
options.B: The company CEO gets a bonus
options.C: Office rent increases

answer_html: Answer: (A) It complies with accounting standards/law or ensures more appropriate presentation of financial statements[cite: 51].

question_html: Accounting policies are based on:

options.A: Various accounting concepts, principles, and conventions
options.B: Political manifestos
options.C: Weather forecasts

answer_html: Answer: (A) Various accounting concepts, principles, and conventions[cite: 51].

question_html: If an inappropriate accounting policy is selected, what is the impact on financial statements according to ICAI study material?

options.A: It could understate or overstate the performance and financial position of a business entity
options.B: It always overstates performance every single time without exception
options.C: It always understates performance every single time without exception

answer_html: Answer: (A) It could understate or overstate the performance and financial position of a business entity[cite: 51].

question_html: Which of the following is NOT one of the three major characteristics considered for the selection of accounting policies?

options.A: Prudence
options.B: Substance over form
options.C: Materiality

answer_html: Answer: (D) Speed of data entry[cite: 51].

question_html: True or False: A change in accounting policies should be made as and when a business likes to show results as per their choice.

options.A: True
options.B: False

answer_html: Answer: (B) False[cite: 51].

question_html: What is the implication if an enterprise charges a proportionate amount of interest to inventory which was earlier not the practice?

options.A: It alters inventory valuation and net profit, requiring quantification and disclosure of the change
options.B: It violates tax laws instantly
options.C: It is classified as an accounting error
options.D: It has no material effect on financial statements

answer_html: Answer: (A) It alters inventory valuation and net profit, requiring quantification and disclosure of the change[cite: 51].

question_html: Which of the following statements is accurate regarding accounting policies?

options.A: They refer to specific principles and methods of applying those principles adopted in financial statement preparation
options.B: They are mandated identical for all companies worldwide
options.C: They are determined solely by bank loan officers
options.D: They never change under any circumstances

answer_html: Answer: (A) They refer to specific principles and methods of applying those principles adopted in financial statement preparation[cite: 51].

question_html: The choice of an appropriate accounting policy calls for:

options.A: Considerate judgement by the management
options.B: A random coin toss
options.C: Strict orders from customers

answer_html: Answer: (A) Considerate judgement by the management[cite: 51].

question_html: Why must the effect of a change in accounting policy be quantified in the financial statements?

options.A: Because without quantification, financial statements may not help users of accounts evaluate performance accurately
options.B: Because tax authorities charge a penalty for unquantified policies
options.C: To inflate asset totals for bank loans

answer_html: Answer: (A) Because without quantification, financial statements may not help users of accounts evaluate performance accurately[cite: 51].

question_html: In valuation of shares or investments held at the end of an accounting period, an enterprise might choose methods such as:

options.A: FIFO, average method, etc.
options.B: Depreciation straight-line method only
options.C: Cash-basis estimation only

answer_html: Answer: (A) FIFO, average method, etc.[cite: 51].

question_html: Which of the following is true regarding areas where different accounting policies are encountered?

options.A: The list provided in standards is illustrative, not exhaustive
options.B: There are exactly three policies in existence worldwide
options.C: Inventories and investments are the only two items allowed in accounting

answer_html: Answer: (A) The list provided in standards is illustrative, not exhaustive[cite: 51].

question_html: When inventories are valued at cost except for finished goods (valued at lower of cost or market value) and by-products (valued at net realizable value), this represents:

options.A: Selection from a set of accounting policies based on specific circumstances
options.B: A violation of accounting standards
options.C: An illegal manipulation of accounts

answer_html: Answer: (A) Selection from a set of accounting policies based on specific circumstances[cite: 51].

question_html: What is the potential consequence of selecting an inappropriate accounting policy on a continuous basis across multiple years?

options.A: Persistent distortion of the entity's reported financial performance and position
options.B: Automatic correction by software after 3 years
options.C: Tax refunds from the government

answer_html: Answer: (A) Persistent distortion of the entity's reported financial performance and position[cite: 51].

question_html: True or False: Selection of an inappropriate accounting policy decision will overstate the performance and financial position of a business entity every time.

options.A: True
options.B: False

answer_html: Answer: (B) False (it could either understate or overstate performance and financial position)[cite: 51].

question_html: Which of the following describes accounting policies in terms of principles and methods?

options.A: Specific principles and methods of applying those principles
options.B: General economic theories unrelated to accounting
options.C: Tax calculation formulas set by parliament

answer_html: Answer: (A) Specific principles and methods of applying those principles[cite: 51].

question_html: If a company changes its accounting policy for inventory valuation from weighted average to FIFO, what effect does this typically have on financial statements?

options.A: It may increase or decrease net profit and inventory valuation depending on price trends
options.B: It always increases net profit by exactly 50%
options.C: It has no numerical impact on profit

answer_html: Answer: (A) It may increase or decrease net profit and inventory valuation depending on price trends[cite: 51].

question_html: What role do regulatory agencies and government play alongside ICAI regarding accounting policies?

options.A: Jointly working in combined efforts to reduce the number of acceptable accounting policies
options.B: Encouraging completely unregulated and chaotic policy selection
options.C: Prohibiting the use of balance sheets
options.D: Mandating cash-only accounting for all enterprises

answer_html: Answer: (A) Jointly working in combined efforts to reduce the number of acceptable accounting policies[cite: 51].

question_html: Which of the following is an area where different accounting policies are frequently encountered?

options.A: Valuation of Inventories
options.B: Employee recruitment policies
options.C: Office cleaning schedules

answer_html: Answer: (A) Valuation of Inventories[cite: 51].

question_html: If an enterprise discloses an inappropriate accounting treatment in the footnotes of its financial statements, what is the legal and accounting status of that disclosure?

options.A: Disclosure is required, but it does not rectify or legalize the inappropriate treatment
options.B: Disclosure completely legalizes the treatment
options.C: Disclosure waives all audit requirements
options.D: Disclosure converts a liability into an asset

answer_html: Answer: (A) Disclosure is required, but it does not rectify or legalize the inappropriate treatment[cite: 51].

question_html: From the perspective of various users of accounts, why must accounting policies be selected with due care?

options.A: Because choices affect performance measurement and financial position as perceived by stakeholders
options.B: Because users audit the books themselves
options.C: To satisfy personal preferences of bank managers
options.D: To avoid paying any income tax

answer_html: Answer: (A) Because choices affect performance measurement and financial position as perceived by stakeholders[cite: 51].

question_html: Which of the following is an example of an investment valuation policy mentioned in the text?

options.A: Long-term investments valued at acquisition cost with provision for permanent diminution
options.B: Investments valued at daily lottery results
options.C: Investments written off immediately as charitable donations
options.D: Investments recorded at future anticipated market peaks

answer_html: Answer: (A) Long-term investments valued at acquisition cost with provision for permanent diminution[cite: 51].

question_html: What is the primary reason why an enterprise cannot use a universal, static list of accounting policies for all operations?

options.A: Diversity and complexity of operating environments require tailored policies
options.B: Statutory laws forbid using the same policy for more than one year
options.C: Auditors charge higher fees for static policies
options.D: Accounting software crashes if policies are universal

answer_html: Answer: (A) Diversity and complexity of operating environments require tailored policies[cite: 51].

question_html: When Omega Enterprises revised its policy to include production overheads in inventory valuation, what was their stated belief?

options.A: It would result in a more appropriate presentation of its financial statements
options.B: It would reduce their tax liability to zero
options.C: It would double their share price overnight
options.D: It would eliminate the need for auditing

answer_html: Answer: (A) It would result in a more appropriate presentation of its financial statements[cite: 51].

question_html: True or False: Valuation of investments is an area where different accounting policies are frequently encountered.

options.A: True
options.B: False

answer_html: Answer: (A) True[cite: 51].

question_html: How does the selection of accounting policies interact with the preparation of the Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss Account?

options.A: Policies directly determine the values assigned to assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses, thereby shaping the reported financial results
options.B: Policies are only used for tax filings and have no connection to financial statements
options.C: Policies are applied after financial statements are finalized
options.D: Policies are strictly decorative and optional

answer_html: Answer: (A) Policies directly determine the values assigned to assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses, thereby shaping the reported financial results[cite: 51].

question_html: Which principle aligns with valuing finished goods at lower of cost or market value?

options.A: Prudence
options.B: Going concern
options.C: Consistency

answer_html: Answer: (A) Prudence[cite: 51].

question_html: What is the main purpose of Unit 5 in the CA Foundation Accounting study material?

options.A: To understand accounting policies, selection criteria, and conditions for changes
options.B: To teach advanced corporate tax auditing
options.C: To review partnership dissolution laws

answer_html: Answer: (A) To understand accounting policies, selection criteria, and conditions for changes[cite: 51].

question_html: If a company changes its accounting policy without statutory requirement or justification for more appropriate presentation, how would auditors likely view it?

options.A: As an unjustified change that may warrant a qualified audit opinion
options.B: As a standard routine procedure
options.C: As an automatic tax credit
options.D: As an enhancement of share value

answer_html: Answer: (A) As an unjustified change that may warrant a qualified audit opinion[cite: 51].

question_html: By-products in inventory valuation are commonly valued at:

options.A: Net realizable value
options.B: Original historical cost of the parent product plus 100%
options.C: Zero value always

answer_html: Answer: (A) Net realizable value[cite: 51].

question_html: What are the three core considerations highlighted in the unit overview diagram for the selection of accounting policies?

options.A: Prudence, Substance over form, Materiality
options.B: Cost, Revenue, Profit
options.C: Assets, Liabilities, Equity

answer_html: Answer: (A) Prudence, Substance over form, Materiality[cite: 51].
